purpose: Student-facing rigorous derivations that expand Chewi's Chapter 1 source statements without changing their provenance or completion status.

entries.title: Proposition 1.1.13 — canonical localization, with the hidden measure theory exposed
entries.scope_note: This is an ASTIS rigorous expansion of Chewi's localization argument. It proves the localization component itself; Proposition 1.1.16 additionally needs random-stopping consistency and cross-horizon gluing, which are now compiled in a separate source-facing route.
formula_latex: \[\tau_c\le t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T\le t\ \text{ or }\ c\le\widehat A_t.\]

proof_steps.title: 1. Complete the exceptional set instead of ignoring it
proof_steps.body: Local square integrability is only almost sure. The bad set N has measure zero, but a stopping-time proof needs a representative defined at every sample point. Under the usual completeness condition, N belongs to every time sigma-algebra. ASTIS replaces the bad energy paths by the zero path, producing a fixed-time measurable representative whose path is continuous and monotone for every omega.

proof_steps.title: 2. Use an equality-level set, not a vague first crossing
proof_steps.body: For c>=0, continuity makes E_c closed. If the level is reached, the infimum of E_c is therefore itself a member of E_c. If the level is never reached, tau_c is defined to be T. This exact equality-level construction is what later prevents an overshoot in the stopped energy.

proof_steps.title: 3. The intermediate value theorem supplies the missing hitting time
proof_steps.body: Suppose c<=Ahat_t and t<=T. Since Ahat_0=0<=c and the completed energy path is continuous, the intermediate value theorem yields s in [0,t] with Ahat_s=c. This is the analytic step hidden inside the usual informal phrase 'first time the energy reaches c'.

proof_steps.title: 4. Turn the analytic definition into a stopping-time event
proof_steps.body: The key equivalence tau_c<=t iff T<=t or c<=Ahat_t converts an infimum-defined random time into a fixed-time threshold event. When t<T the deterministic alternative disappears, so measurability follows from fixed-time measurability of Ahat_t. This is the filtration-level reason tau_c is a stopping time.

proof_steps.title: 5. Prove no overshoot, including the fallback case
proof_steps.body: If E_c is nonempty, Ahat_{tau_c}=c because tau_c belongs to the equality-level set. If E_c is empty and Ahat_T were larger than c, continuity would force an equality-level time, contradiction. Hence Ahat_{tau_c}<=c in both cases.

proof_steps.title: 6. Stop the integrand progressively and identify its exact energy
proof_steps.body: ASTIS stops the completed integrand using the observable threshold Ahat_s<c. Before T, continuity and monotonicity prove Ahat_s<c iff s<tau_c. The single endpoint s=T is null for the time measure, so the time integral of the stopped square is exactly Ahat_{tau_c}, and is therefore at most c.

proof_steps.title: 7. Choose c=n+1 and show the sequence exhausts the horizon
proof_steps.body: Higher energy levels cannot be hit earlier. For each completed path, the terminal energy is a finite real number; once n+1 exceeds it, the equality-level set is empty and tau_n=T. Thus tau_n is increasing and is eventually exactly T pathwise, hence converges to T. Under a probability law, the pathwise bound also gives the global product-L2 integrability needed by the Itô map.

subtle_points: The completion step is mathematically substantive: an almost-surely continuous energy path is not enough for defining a stopping time pointwise on every omega.
Using the equality-level set plus continuity is what proves no overshoot. A raw infimum of a strict crossing set needs a separate boundary argument.
The thresholded integrand is defined by Ahat_s<c because this event is progressive/measurable. Its equality with stopping before tau_c is then proved, not assumed.
The terminal point T is discarded only inside a time integral, where the singleton has zero Lebesgue measure; it is not silently removed from pointwise statements.

entries.title: Display (1.1.14) — why every energy truncation is an honest continuous martingale
entries.scope_note: This display applies the already-constructed global L2 Ito integral to the canonical energy truncation. The display itself gives deterministic-time restriction compatibility, not arbitrary random-stopping consistency; that extra bridge belongs to Proposition 1.1.16 and is now compiled separately.

proof_steps.title: 1. Proposition 1.1.13 converts local L2 into global L2
proof_steps.body: The pathwise energy bound at level n+1 makes the stopped integrand square integrable on Omega x [0,T] under a probability measure. This is the exact hypothesis needed by the global Itô construction already formalized in Theorem 1.1.8.

proof_steps.title: 2. Reuse the global Itô map; do not invent a second integral
proof_steps.body: canonicalStoppedItoProcess is literally itoIntegralProcess applied to canonicalStoppedProgressiveL2. Therefore strong adaptedness, the martingale property, and continuous paths are inherited from the global L2 theory rather than reproved by an unrelated construction.
proof_steps.formula_latex: \[\eta^{(n)}\in L^2_{\mathrm{prog}}(\Omega\times[0,T])\quad\Longrightarrow\quad M^{(n)}=I(\eta^{(n)})\text{ is an adapted continuous martingale}.\]

proof_steps.title: 3. Deterministic-time restriction compatibility
proof_steps.body: At each deterministic t<=T, the process value agrees almost surely with the terminal L2 Itô integral of the same stopped integrand restricted to [0,t]. This gives a single coherent process-level version rather than unrelated L2 random variables at each time.

subtle_points: An energy-truncated integrand being globally L2 is enough to construct M^(n), but it is not yet the statement M_{t wedge tau_n}=M_t^(n).

For a random tau inside an elementary grid cell, the final Brownian increment must be cut at tau; multiplying the whole cell coefficient by 1_{t_i<tau} alone does not prove the stochastic-integral stopping identity.

The required grid-valued stopping, dyadic approximation, L2/continuous-path passage, stopping-graph nullity, cross-horizon overlap, and pathwise gluing steps are now compiled and assembled in Proposition 1.1.16.
